owner_brief: The owner, 2026-10-10: "any Pokemon caught should count as a resource, so the clock should run faster. We will need a system to weigh all valuables, like 20 coal or a diamond is 1 point, and 2 points is +0.1x faster or something." And (staging, same day): ore mined in a wall did not count, and "it should".
unit: cp, a hundredth of a point. 1 point = 100 cp = $100 of the economy's prices (the owner's two anchors sit at $80 and $120 a point, so $100 is between them and each anchor is pinned exactly)

bank_removed: its last price in base_removed / buys_removed (taken off for arbitrage, still worth it)

derived: from a recipe or trade that links it to a priced item; or (DUNGEON_VAULTS, 2026-10-11) for an item nothing sells, from the price of the sold item of its class, the class and the item named in the row (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_VAULTS.md 3)

rate.why: the owner's +0.1x per 2 points. units_per_tick (data/dungeons.json engine.clock) is 10, so x1 is 10 and each 0.1x is one unit: rate = 10 + floor(cp / 200). catches.kinds_why: which room the catch was made in (the catcher's position at the pokemon_captured callback; the caught entity is gone by then, docs/research/notes/dungeon-catches-on-the-clock.md section 6). Anywhere that is not a nest, miniboss or habitat room counts as ambient
catches.why: A catch is the owner's resource. The anchor is the owner's own "catch ten [a nest], and the run gets urgent" (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_CATCHES.md 1 and 4: ten catches was x1.5): ten nest catches at 1 point are 10 points, x1.5. A band's ambient and nest Pokemon are a later stage of their line higher up (tools/dungeon_life.py stage_of), so 1.5 points at bands 3-4 and 2 at 5-6. A mini-boss is an ordinary catch (the owner, 2026-10-10: every dungeon Pokemon is catchable, at ordinary values), weighed as a nest's. DESIGN numbers: trainer-balance-designer's to tune

habitat.why: A habitat holds the dungeon's PRIZE (the owner, 2026-10-10). Before the Beast Ball stage it is a rare non-legendary (a pseudo-legendary's middle stage, such as a Gabite; pass 3 chooses it): 8 points, +0.4x, eight ordinary catches, because it is the rarest thing the run offers and it is optional. From that band on it is a legendary or an Ultra Beast: 20 points, +1.0x alone, so a run that takes it runs the rest of its clock at least twice as fast. The room is about 6 minutes of fight (tools/dungeon_clock.py HABITAT_S); the clock says what the prize is worth. DESIGN numbers, below the cap (40 points) so a prize never ends a run on its own

not_counted.relics: a relic (tools/dungeon_relics.py) has no economy by design and rewards finding a secret; counting it would tax the exploration it pays for
not_counted.escrow: the boss and stand payouts are paid at a clean exit, after the clock (DUNGEONS.md 9.1)
not_counted.drops: items a wild Pokemon drops in a run are not measured: no source event is proven for them (a minecraft.picked_up stat is a candidate, untested)

vault_budget.dollar_factor_why: DECIDED by the owner 2026-10-11: double it; a richer vault should cost more clock, that is the greed mechanic working. DUNGEON_VAULTS (2026-10-11), the owner: 'I think the vault isn't rewarding enough.' At 1.0 a chest held 80-370 cp, under one Great Ball (350) at bands 1-4, so no vault could hold a ball a chest. At 2.0 a vault may pay twice the run's time gathering: it costs a code or a dead end, 20-45 s of clock a chest, and the GREED charge of its expected value, which gathering does not. Nothing a vault now gives sells to the bank (data/bank.json buys only minerals), so the extra value is balls, held items and candy, not money; the one cash route is the wishing well (2 throws a run, expected share 0.9 or under). The owner's to confirm (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_VAULTS.md 7)
vault_budget.why: GREED found vault chests worth 7 to 150 points (one can cap the clock). A vault's chests together are worth at most dollar_factor x the gathering tier open at the band's lowest badge count x the required hours of the dungeon the vault stands in (its own clock over the 1.25 slack; MEGA-INTEGRATE 2026-10-11, tools/dungeon_greed.py vault_budget(doc, table, dungeon): until then the shortest rooms dungeon's, so a new short dungeon shrank every other dungeon's vaults and authors padded their clocks to avoid it): the limit RESOURCES2 set for a resources room (tools/dungeon_resources.py budget(), every price and rate read from tools/economy_sim.py World), so a vault never pays more than the same run's time spent gathering, which costs no sigil, no clock and no death. A chest's budget is the vault's over its chest count; its value is GREED's chest_cp (the expected cp of its loot at the band). With the kit's four chests and the Night Shift's own clocks (2026-10-11) at dollar_factor 1.0: 82, 189, 189, 198, 346, 367 cp a chest at bands 1-6; at 2.0 (DUNGEON_VAULTS): 165, 378, 378, 396, 692, 734 (each dungeon's figure moves with its own clock only; DUNGEON_ROOMS.md 1b).
vault_budget.enforce_why: true since DG3-INTEGRATE (2026-10-10): problems() refuses a chest over budget. DUNGEON_VAULTS (2026-10-11) re-authored every vault and bank vault to about 90% of the dollar_factor-2 budget (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_VAULTS.md 2), computed by hand, not by the tool: the orchestrator's python tools/dungeon_greed.py run is the check.
